title: Man, 26, victim of fatal police shooting on Whitefish Lake First Nation
article: A 26-year-old man shot and killed by an RCMP officer at Whitefish Lake First Nation was reportedly swinging a knife, says the province\'s police watchdog.

St. Paul RCMP were called to a disturbance on the Whitefish First Nation 180 km northeast of Edmonton around 6:15 p.m. Sept. 6, said the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) in a Friday news release.

The first officer on scene, making his way from St. Paul which is about 60 kilometres southeast of the scene, arrived at 7:45 p.m. and saw a man walking on the side of a road. The officer stepped out of his police vehicle and attempted to speak to the man, who was carrying a knife, says ASIRT.
A "confrontation" began that ended with the lone officer firing his police service weapon at the man who was "critically" injured, according to ASIRT.
The officer and others who arrived on scene shortly after gave the man emergency medical treatment until EMS crews arrived. The man was transported to hospital but died of his injuries on the way.
ASIRT investigates cases where police have injured or killed civilians, as well as serious allegations of police misconduct.
